issues.failure_explanation: The cellwise integration by parts over the bounded cylinder also produces lateral boundary terms on $\partial\Omega\times(0,T)$. The support assumption controls only the exact solution (and test functions constructed from it), not the minimizer $u_{\theta^*}$; the loss contains no spatial boundary penalty and the network class imposes no boundary condition. Hence the claimed cancellation is unsupported. For instance, with Burgers flux an entropy wave entering through the spatial boundary can have zero initial error and nonpositive interior Kruzhkov production, hence loss $O(h)$ after smoothing, while producing an $O(1)$ final-time error.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \item on a compound-wave piece, the local construction as in Theorem~\ref{thm:compound_wave};

issues.failure_explanation: A compound wave couples an entropy shock to an attached rarefaction fan. The shock proof requires a shifted interface and strip selection, while the rarefaction proof uses the fan singularity. The coupling terms, such as the shifted shock trace against the rarefaction-side gradient, are treated in neither proof, and no appendix proof is supplied, so the stated rate is unsupported.

failure_location.quote: The proof follows the same strategy as a single shock (Theorem~\ref{thm:shock}) and a single rarefaction (Theorem~\ref{thm:rarefaction}), so we omit the details.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Provide the missing compound-wave competitor and test-function construction, including the balance of shifted-interface and rarefaction-fan terms. If the sharp square-root-log rate is not obtained, state the provable bound; the main 1D theorem only requires a bound no worse than $O(h^{1/2}|\ln h|)$.
issues.overall_effect: The compound-wave convergence rate is not established, and the proof of the general 1D main theorem, which explicitly uses the missing compound-wave construction, is incomplete for solutions containing compound waves.
issues.title: Compound-wave convergence theorem is stated without a proof
issues.why_classification: A contained but nontrivial local argument is missing; a comparable result, possibly with a slightly weakened rate, remains available without changing the global proof architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where \(\sigma=\tanh\) acts componentwise, \(W_\ell\) and \(b_\ell\) denote the weight matrix and bias vector, respectively

issues.failure_explanation: The surrogate contains the product $(r-s)\tanh(\tau(r-s))$. A layer of the network in \eqref{def:NN} is an affine map followed by componentwise $\tanh$; such layers cannot multiply two previously computed quantities, nor pass an affine factor through to multiply an activation. Therefore $S_{\min,\tau}$ is not a composition of affine maps and $\tanh$ in the sense of the stated architecture, and the claimed exact realization is unsupported.

failure_location.quote: Since \(S_{\min,\tau}\) and \(S_{\max,\tau}\) are compositions of affine maps and \(\tanh\), each \(\varphi_{j,\tau}\) is realized by a \(\tanh\) network with the same asymptotic depth and width bounds.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must either change the network class or activation so that the smooth min/max units are exactly representable, or prove a new approximation theorem showing ordinary tanh feedforward networks approximate these units to the required accuracy with the same depth and width scaling.
issues.overall_effect: The existence of the claimed tanh competitors with small loss is not established. Consequently, every loss bound and convergence result that obtains its competitor through Lemma~\ref{lem:loss_cpwl_approx} is unproven for the stated tanh network class.
